audit.whatIsWrong: Sanguine Pool is named as the matchup-defining cooldown in both layers and neither ever gives its number.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28/25/22/19/16s. At rank 1 that is a twenty-eight second window, and Vladimir players almost never rank W early because it costs health and does no damage. "Bait the pool" is correct advice with no teeth until the reader knows how long the reward lasts. This is the single most useful number in the matchup and it was absent from both layers.
audit.corrected: Sanguine Pool 28/25/22/19/16s with 2 seconds of untargetability — a spent pool is a half-minute of free lane.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json — W Sanguine Pool cooldown and description

audit.whatIsWrong: Transfusion is described in the content layer as "his Q heals him" with no cooldown, and never appears in the full layer.
audit.why: Transfusion runs 9/7.9/6.8/5.7/4.6s. That scaling is the whole early lane: at rank 1 there is a real nine-second gap where his sustain is down and Nasus can walk up, and by rank 5 there is effectively no gap at all. Without the numbers the reader has no way to pick the moment.
audit.corrected: Transfusion 9s at rank 1 falling to 4.6s — trade inside the rank-1 gap while it still exists.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer said Fury of the Sands "flips dives" at level 6, with no mention of the pool.
audit.why: Fury of the Sands is a persistent aura that ticks damage around Nasus. Sanguine Pool makes Vladimir untargetable for two seconds. Opening the all-in with R means a large part of the ultimate duration ticks while he is in the puddle. The content layer already gets this right; the full layer contradicted it by presenting R as the opener.
audit.corrected: Wither and bait the pool first, ult second. Never lead the all-in with Fury of the Sands.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nasus.json — R Fury of the Sands, zone flag

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer gives Vladimir stages 1-5 including level 1 at 8/10, and its phases[0] says "Vladimir wins every level-1 exchange". The content layer says the opposite in whys[0]: neither champion owns the opener.
audit.why: Vladimir has one damaging spell at level 1, no resource cost pressure and no early kill threat; Nasus is equally weak. Calling it an 8/10 enemy-favoured stage tells a Nasus to concede a lane opener he does not need to concede. Nasus wins the matchup 50.26% over 949 games.
audit.corrected: phases[0].why rewritten to match. The side tokens could not be flipped: "Vladimir" is 8 characters against "Skill"/"Nasus" at 5, so every swap fails the ±10% band. phases[0], [3] should read Skill and phases[2], [4], [5] should read Nasus per the content chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1] tells the reader not to "Stack pure HP" and then gives a generic reason about wasting cooldowns that has nothing to do with health.
audit.why: The real reason is that Hemoplague amplifies the damage its targets take, and Vladimir is fully magic damage — magic resist reduces the incoming number, raw health does not. Separately, Crimson Pact means the health Vladimir buys becomes ability power, which is worth knowing when reading his build but is not a reason to change yours.
audit.corrected: Magic resist over another health item; the reason is Hemoplague amplification, not cooldown economy.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json — R Hemoplague, P Crimson Pact

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds named, despite two of his abilities healing him.
audit.why: Transfusion heals on every cast and Hemoplague heals him for each champion hit. Against a Nasus grinding with Soul Eater lifesteal, unanswered healing on a 4.6s cooldown decides the extended fight.
audit.corrected: Flagged. The natural home is the itemization string, which lives inside report[] and is not safely addressable by path.

edits.before: Q start, last-hit only. Vladimir wins every level-1 exchange — concede the bush, concede the trades, take the stacks.
edits.after: Q start, last-hit only. Nobody wins level 1 here — Vladimir is one of the weakest openers in the game, so just bank stacks.

edits.before: Wither online — it's your get-off-me button, not a kill tool yet. Hold it for Vladimir's engage, never open with it.
edits.after: Transfusion heals him on a 9s cooldown at rank 1 — trade inside that gap, because by rank 5 it is back every 4.6s.

edits.before: E lets you stack safely from range when Vladimir zones you. Spirit Fire the wave under tower; every stack denied is his only real win condition.
edits.after: Wither is online: the instant he steps up to poke, slow him and walk him down. Spirit Fire the wave so his push cannot deny your stacks.

edits.before: Still Vladimir's window — respect Sanguine Pool fully. Passive lifesteal plus Fleet means he must commit hard to actually dent you; make those commits cost.
edits.after: Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 and only 2s of untargetability — most Vlads leave it at one point, so a baited pool hands you half a minute of free lane.

edits.before: Fury of the Sands flips dives: pop R, Wither Vladimir, and suddenly the stat-check runs your way. First real fight you're allowed to take.
edits.after: Never open the all-in with Fury of the Sands — he pools, goes untargetable, and your ult ticks into an empty puddle. Wither, bait, then ult.

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Dodges your Q. Bait it. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: 28/25/22/19/16s — bait it early and you own the next 28 seconds.

edits.before: Dodges your Q. Bait it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 2s untargetable on a 28s rank-1 cooldown — bait it, then commit.

edits.before: Vladimir wastes Sanguine Pool — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Crimson Pact turns his bonus health straight into ability power.

edits.before: That is Vladimir's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Two seconds of untargetability wastes your ult ticks and your empowered Q entirely.

edits.before: Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Against Hemoplague's amp you want magic resist, not another health item.

edits.before: Fury of the Sands plus Wither: your cleanest kill window, but bait Sanguine Pool first or your ult damage hits an untargetable puddle.
edits.after: Fury of the Sands plus Wither: your cleanest kill window, but bait Sanguine Pool first — at rank 1 it is 28s, so a spent pool is a free kill.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a Wither-cooldown coinflip, you're both farming and trading, so neither side cleanly owns it.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 hinge on cooldowns: Wither is 15s at rank 1 and his Transfusion heal is 9s, so time your walk-ups.

notes: I did not write anything based on the Tides of Blood line in champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json — Riot's text says it 'can be blocked by enemy units', which for an ability that damages the area around him is ambiguous enough that I could not tell whether it means minions absorb it, whether it is directional, or whether the text is stale. It would be a genuinely useful piece of lane tech if someone confirms it on the wiki, so it is worth a look rather than a guess.
